//: The store-readiness FLOOR — the harness's half of the store policy since the 1.0.0 split (the consumer's half lives in the seeded tools/store-tunables.json: iosEncryption, privacyAccessedApiTypes, accountDeletion, icons — values that are the PROJECT's reviewed decisions, which an owned sha-pinned file could only call tampering). This file stays OWNED because every value in it is one the harness must be able to ship and correct: check-version-sync reds a missing iosToolchain record and tells the consumer to run `update` to restore it, which only works while `update` may write the file. androidTargetSdk: `floor` is Google Play's rolling target-API requirement, and it is a DATED one — from 2026-08-31 new apps AND app updates must target Android 16 (API 36) or higher to be submitted at all, so the floor moved 35 -> 36 in harness 0.5.0 (reviewed 2026-08-06, 25 days ahead of the deadline; an extension to 2026-11-01 is requestable in the Play Console but is a per-developer act this file cannot assume). Wear OS / Automotive stay at 35 and TV / XR at 34 — a project shipping one of those form factors lowers this floor deliberately, in a reviewed commit, which is what this file being reviewed data is for. SOURCE: https://developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk. expoSdkDefaults maps an Expo SDK major to the targetSdkVersion it ships when the config declares none (SDK 57 targets 36, so a stock scaffold already satisfies the raised floor and only a config that pinned 35 by hand goes red) — an UNKNOWN SDK major fails closed until a human pins it. usageDescriptionKeysByPlugin: which InfoPlist purpose strings a config plugin implies — the pre-prebuild surface (a bare npm dep without a plugin is invisible until prebuild; Apple's post-submission validation remains the backstop). trackingSdkSignals: plugin/dependency names that mean the app tracks — with none present, an ATT string or NSPrivacyTracking declaration is an unreviewed tracking claim and reds; with one present, all three declarations must agree. iosToolchain: the Apple BUILD-TOOLCHAIN floor the version-sync gate holds over eas.json's production ios.image — xcodeFloor is the minimum `-xcode-<major>` a CONCRETE pinned image name must carry, inForceSince/source cite the requirement, and the enforcement-tiers version-sync Target discharges through this record (its `closes:` probe names this key).

iosToolchain.why: Apple requires uploads to build against Xcode 26 / iOS 26 SDK or later — a FIXED floor in force since 2026-04-28, not a moving 'current SDK' requirement, and macOS is excluded. Only a concrete pinned image name matching -xcode-<major> is statically checkable: auto, latest, sdk-NN and an absent pin are unverifiable and must not read as green, because a check that passes an unpinned profile passes every profile.
